## 29. Core types

The wire shapes from `@harness/core` that the SDK's declarations refer to, each resolved to plain TypeScript. Each is a
zod schema in core with its type inferred from it; import the type (and the schema, to parse) from `@harness/core`.

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/access.ts`

Whether the hub has more than one person; the web shows visibility controls only when it does.


#### <a id="core-approvalpreview"></a>`ApprovalPreview`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/approvals.ts`

What a run would do, worked out before it is approved.

```ts
type ApprovalPreview = {
  title: string;
  parts: ({
    type: "text";
    text: string;
  } | {
    type: "code";
    language: string;
    code: string;
    title?: string | undefined;
  } | {
    type: "table";
    title: string;
    table: {
      columns: {
        name: string;
        kind: "number" | "boolean" | "date" | "text" | "integer" | "datetime" | "time" | "uuid" | "json" | "binary";
        nullable: boolean;
        label?: string | undefined;
        type?: TypeDef<any> | undefined;
        ref?: `${string}/${string}` | undefined;
      }[];
      rows: z.core.util.JSONType[][];
      offset: number;
      truncated: boolean;
      sort: {
        column: string;
        dir: "asc" | "desc";
      }[];
      limit?: number | undefined;
      total?: number | undefined;
    };
  } | {
    type: "type-diff";
    name: string;
    changes: string[];
    breaks: {
      fn: string;
      why: string;
    }[];
    before?: TypeDef<any> | undefined;
    after?: TypeDef<any> | undefined;
  })[];
  irreversible: boolean;
  subject?: {
    kind: "system-install";
    system: string & z.core.$brand<"SystemName">;
    instance: string & z.core.$brand<"InstanceName">;
    version: string;
    manifestHash: string;
    bundleHash: string;
    sourceHash: string;
    host: {
      system: string & z.core.$brand<"SystemName">;
      instance: string & z.core.$brand<"InstanceName">;
    };
    replaces?: {
      version: string;
      manifestHash: string;
    } | undefined;
  } | undefined;
};
```

#### <a id="core-contextdecl"></a>`ContextDecl`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/manifest.ts`

A context item. `name` is its stable key (`authoring.kinds`): readable, never shown to people, never derived from a
file path, so the hub updates the same record (links, stats, embeddings) when its title, text or place change.

```ts
type ContextDecl = {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  imports: `${string}/${string}`[];
  fns: `${string}/${string}`[];
  suggestFns: `${string}/${string}`[];
  suggest: "llm" | "none" | "user" | "both";
  visible: "llm" | "none" | "user" | "both";
  alwaysFor: `${string}/${string}`[];
  tags: string[];
  title?: string | undefined;
  content?: string | undefined;
  command?: {
    name: string;
    args: {
      name: string;
      hint: string;
      required: boolean;
    }[];
  } | undefined;
  weight?: number | undefined;
  summary?: string | undefined;
  parent?: `${string}/${string}` | undefined;
  next?: `${string}/${string}` | undefined;
  choices?: {
    to: `${string}/${string}`;
    when: string;
  }[] | undefined;
  links?: {
    to: {
      kind: "context";
      name: `${string}/${string}`;
    } | {
      kind: "fn";
      name: `${string}/${string}`;
    } | {
      kind: "type";
      name: `${string}/${string}`;
    } | {
      kind: "resource";
      uri: `${string}://${string}`;
      section?: (string & z.core.$brand<"SectionKey">) | undefined;
    };
    relation: "next" | "about" | "parent" | "imports" | "brings" | "suggests" | "related";
    weight: number;
  }[] | undefined;
};
```

#### <a id="core-contextfileheader"></a>`ContextFileHeader`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/context-files.ts`

The YAML header of a context file: `ContextDecl` without its content (the body is the content), with `key` for its
name and the lists optional. A summary is required, so every item has a short form for small models. Every link
(`fns`, `imports`, `choices`, `links`, `parent`, `next`, `alwaysFor`) is a qualified name.

```ts
type ContextFileHeader = {
  description: string;
  key: string;
  summary: string;
  imports: `${string}/${string}`[];
  fns: `${string}/${string}`[];
  suggestFns: `${string}/${string}`[];
  suggest: "llm" | "none" | "user" | "both";
  visible: "llm" | "none" | "user" | "both";
  alwaysFor: `${string}/${string}`[];
  tags: string[];
  title?: string | undefined;
  weight?: number | undefined;
  next?: `${string}/${string}` | undefined;
  links?: {
    to: {
      kind: "context";
      name: `${string}/${string}`;
    } | {
      kind: "fn";
      name: `${string}/${string}`;
    } | {
      kind: "type";
      name: `${string}/${string}`;
    } | {
      kind: "resource";
      uri: `${string}://${string}`;
      section?: (string & z.core.$brand<"SectionKey">) | undefined;
    };
    relation: "next" | "about" | "parent" | "imports" | "brings" | "suggests" | "related";
    weight: number;
  }[] | undefined;
  command?: {
    name: string;
    args: {
      name: string;
      hint: string;
      required: boolean;
    }[];
  } | undefined;
  parent?: `${string}/${string}` | undefined;
  choices?: {
    to: `${string}/${string}`;
    when: string;
  }[] | undefined;
};
```

#### <a id="core-costestimate"></a>`CostEstimate`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/fn-facts.ts`

What a call is expected to cost, in dollars. `basis` says where the numbers come from: `free` (nothing it does
spends), `history` (its settled runs), `payload` (worked out from the call's args and the model's price), or
`unknown` (it spends and has never run).

```ts
type CostEstimate = {
  min: number;
  typical: number;
  max: number;
  basis: "unknown" | "history" | "payload" | "free";
  runs: number;
};
```

#### <a id="core-decideanswer"></a>`DecideAnswer`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/decisions.ts`

The answer. `decision`: the model's picks, best first (none means make something new), with its reasons.
`off`: no decision model is set, so go by the scores. `failed`: it was set but its call failed, so go by the scores.

```ts

  by: "decision";
  picked: {
    id: string;
    why?: string | undefined;
  }[];
  note?: string | undefined;
  call?: string | undefined;
} | {
  by: "off";
} | {
  by: "failed";
  message: string;
};
```

#### <a id="core-fneffects"></a>`FnEffects`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/manifest.ts`

What a fn says it does to data (`FnDecl.effects`): its mode, the named types it reads and writes, and whether its
own work costs nothing. Absent parts are worked out by the hub (`FnFacts`): the mode from the `read` tag, the types
from its signature, and everything a fn uses (its deps, an agent's tools) is folded in.

```ts
type FnEffects = {
  mode?: "read" | "write" | "delete" | undefined;
  reads?: `${string}/${string}`[] | undefined;
  writes?: `${string}/${string}`[] | undefined;
  free?: boolean | undefined;
};
```

#### <a id="core-fnrouting"></a>`FnRouting`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/manifest.ts`

Build 5: which instance of a fleet runs a fn's calls. `instance`: always that one (a database's query fns), and the
fn belongs to it the way `TypeDecl.instance` says. `any`: whichever connected instance the hub picks first (the
session's pin, then the default), with no ambiguity refusal; the fn forwards with `on` itself when it must.
Absent: the fleet rules (`FleetRouter`).

```ts
type FnRouting = {
  to: "instance";
  instance: string & z.core.$brand<"InstanceName">;
} | {
  to: "any";
};
```

#### <a id="core-fnsearchquery"></a>`FnSearchQuery`

const, type · declared in `packages/core/src/fn-facts.ts`

A search over fns and context, done in the hub's database. Without `text` it lists what the filters let through,
by name. Every filter narrows: `kinds` (the fn kinds, such as `input/form` or `database/query`), `systems`,
`instance` (a fleet instance's own fns), `visibility` (what the asker shares: `mine` they own, `shared` others gave
them), `types` (fns that read or write any of these named types), `modes` (fns of these modes), and `names` (exactly
these fns and context items, to look up their hits by name).

```ts
type FnSearchQuery = {
  text?: string | undefined;
```
